reuse.why: Adds one skip-set helper that every month-wide action consults and keeps using setBudget/batchMessages; it does not reuse the averaging actions' existing hidden-filtering query but leaves it in place alongside the new check.

duplication.why: The protection rule itself is defined once, but the three averaging actions keep their own copy of the category query with `c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0`, so the hidden rule is now applied twice there, and the skip check is pasted into five loops.

placement.why: The helper lives in budget/actions.ts beside getBudgetData and the actions it serves.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, tests and a release note are touched; single-category actions are left alone.

maintainability.why: One SQL helper owns the skip rule, which is easy to change, though the redundant hidden filters and the separate per-action category queries remain for a maintainer to reconcile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All five month-wide actions consult getCategoryIdsSkippedByMonthWideActions.

disguised_duplication.where: The leftover hidden filters in set3MonthAvg/set6MonthAvg/set12MonthAvg SQL are pre-existing and unchanged, not reshaped.

one_place.where: getCategoryIdsSkippedByMonthWideActions in budget/actions.ts is used by copyPreviousMonth, setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg; the averaging actions' own SQL still also filters hidden categories redundantly.
